</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt"><B>Vale concludes aluminum portfolio management</B>
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">Rio de Janeiro, February&nbsp;28, 2011 &#151; Vale S.A. (Vale) informs that it has concluded the
transaction announced on May&nbsp;2, 2010, with Norsk Hydro ASA (Hydro), a company listed
on the Oslo Stock Exchange and the London Stock Exchange (ticker symbol: NHY), transferring
its stakes in Albras &#151;  Alum&#237;nio Brasileiro S.A. (Albras), Alunorte  &#151;  Alumina do Norte do
Brasil S.A. (Alunorte) and Companhia de Alumina do Par&#225; (CAP), along with its
respective off-take rights and outstanding commercial contracts and net debt of US$655
million for 22% of Hydro&#146;s common shares outstanding after the shares issued by Hydro
today, and US$503&nbsp;million in cash, after adjustments.
</DIV>

<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">In addition, Vale formed a newly incorporated Minera&#231;&#227;o Paragominas S.A (Paragominas)
and transferred the Paragominas bauxite mine and all its other Brazilian bauxite
mineral rights to this new company. As part of the transaction, Vale sold 60% of
Paragominas to Hydro for US$578&nbsp;million in cash, after working capital adjustments, and the
remaining 40% will be sold in two equal tranches of 20% in 2013 and 2015, for US$200&nbsp;million in
cash each.
</DIV>

<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">Under the terms of the agreement, Vale, through its wholly owned subsidiaries, transferred to
Hydro: (i)&nbsp;51% of the total capital of Albras; (ii)&nbsp;57% of the total capital of
Alunorte; (iii)&nbsp;61% of the total capital of CAP; and sold (iv)&nbsp;60% of the total
capital of Paragominas, in which Vale remains with 40% equity interest until it is fully
divested until 2015.
</DIV>

<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">Vale, through its wholly owned subsidiaries, subscribed 447,834,465 Hydro shares or 22%
of the 2,035,611,206 shares outstanding, valued at approximately US$3.5&nbsp;billion
according to Hydro&#146;s closing share price and NOK exchange rate on February&nbsp;25, 2011.
Pursuant to the transaction agreements, Vale cannot divest its shares during a
two-year lock-up period after the closing or increase its ownership in Hydro beyond its 22%
stake.
</DIV>

<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">As part of the agreement, Vale is entitled to have one representative on Hydro&#146;s Board of
Directors. Tito Martins, our Executive Officer of Base Metals Operations, has been elected as a
board member and joined Hydro&#146;s board with the completion of the transaction.
</DIV>

<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">The combination of Vale and Hydro assets creates one of the world&#146;s largest and most competitive
integrated aluminum companies, with growth potential and access to large bauxite reserves, captive
power generation at competitive prices and technological expertise.
</DIV>

<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">Vale is engaged in active portfolio asset management, which is one of the pillars of our strategy
to create value on a sustainable basis. Given that Vale remains exposed to the
aluminum business through a significant stake in the combined company, we strongly believe that
this transaction will create substantial value for our shareholders.
</DIV>

<DIV align="right" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt"><B>For further information, please contact:</B><BR>
&#043;55-21-3814-4540<BR>
Roberto Castello Branco: roberto.castello.branco@vale.com<BR>
Viktor Moszkowicz: viktor.moszkowicz@vale.com<BR>

Fernando Frey: fernando.frey@vale.com<BR>
Marcio Loures Penna: marcio.penna@vale.com<BR>
Samantha Pons: samantha.pons@vale.com<BR>
Thomaz Freire: thomaz.freire@vale.com
</DIV>


<DIV align="justify" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 10pt">This press release may include statements that present Vale&#146;s expectations about future events or
results. All statements, when based upon expectations about the future and not on historical
facts, involve various risks and uncertainties. Vale cannot guarantee that such statements will
prove correct. These risks and uncertainties include factors related to the following: (a)&nbsp;the countries where we operate,
especially Brazil and Canada; (b)&nbsp;the global economy; (c)&nbsp;the capital markets; (d)&nbsp;the mining and
metals prices and their dependence on global industrial production, which is cyclical by nature;
and (e)&nbsp;global competition in the markets in which Vale operates. To obtain further information on
factors that may lead to results different from those forecast by Vale, please consult the
reports Vale files with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC), the Brazilian Comiss&#227;o de
Valores Mobili&#225;rios (CVM), the French Autorit&#233; des March&#233;s Financiers (AMF), and The Stock Exchange of
Hong Kong Limited, and in particular the factors discussed under &#147;Forward-Looking Statements&#148;
and &#147;Risk Factors&#148; in Vale&#146;s annual report on Form 20-F.
</DIV>
